articles.title: Serie A official line-ups: Lecce vs. Juventus
articles.summary: Juventus start Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani together for the first time in Serie A, desperately trying to get back on track away to unpredictable Lec...
articles.body:
Juventus start Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani together for the first time in Serie A, desperately trying to get back on track away to unpredictable Lecce amid an injury crisis.

It kicks off at the Stadio Via del Mare at 17.00 GMT (18.00 CET).

REGGIO NELL'EMILIA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 13: Luciano Spalletti Head Coach of Juventus looks on prior to the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and Juventus at Mapei Stadium – Citta' del Tricolore on September 13, 2026 in Reggio nell'Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

Luciano Spalletti is really feeling the pressure after a series of dismal results, culminating in the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio.

Things didn't go much better in Thursday's Europa League game, as they fumbled a lead and ultimately scraped the 2-2 draw with Stade Rennais.

That saw the first ever start for the new strike pairing of Woltemade and Kolo Muani, and it is repeated here this evening, with Weston McKennie in a free role behind them.

TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 22: Randal Kolo Muani of Juventus looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Juventus and Stade Rennais FC at Juventus Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

The injury crisis keeps getting worse, with only 17 outfield players making the trip to Lecce.

Nico Gonzalez and Zeki Celik are the latest additions to the absentee list with Kenan Yildiz, Francisco Conceicao, Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Jeff Ekhator and Kamil Grabara.

Pierre Kalulu is therefore pushed into a more advanced role, while Teun Koopmeiners joins Douglas Luiz in midfield.

Juventus midfielder Douglas Luiz in action away to Cagliari (@juventus)

Lecce are an all or nothing team, so far winning three games and losing four without a single stalemate.

They are fresh off a sensational 3-0 victory away to Udinese, but it came at a cost, losing Lassana Coulibaly to a muscular injury.

Santiago Pierotti, Ivan Ilic and Medon Berisha are already out of action, so Ousmane Drame' steps into midfield rather than Mohamed Kaba.

Willem Geubbels is supported by Konan N'Dri and Amar Fatah once again.

Lecce have not beaten Juventus since a 2-0 result here in February 2011, followed by four 1-1 draws and eight defeats, home and away.

UDINE, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Kialonda Gaspar of Lecce celebrates scoring his team's first goal with teammate Konan N'Dri during the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and US Lecce at Stadio Friuli on October 18, 2026 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images)

Lecce: Falcone, Danilo Veiga, Tiago Gabriel, Gaspar, Gallo; Dramé, Ngom, Maleh; N'Dri, Geubbels, Fatah

Juventus: Vicario, Gatti, Bremer, Lucumi; Kalulu, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners, Cambiaso; McKennie; Woltemade, Kolo Muani

articles.title: Javier Romero, chef, y el truco para triunfar con las costillas en la Airfryer: "El secreto está en el adobo, potencia el sabor"
articles.standfirst: La guía definitiva para preparar costillas de cerdo crujientes siguiendo los consejos de los expertos
articles.summary: La guía definitiva para preparar costillas de cerdo crujientes siguiendo los consejos de los expertos
articles.body: La cocina casera se ha transformado por completo con la llegada de las freidoras de aire, convirtiéndose en el electrodoméstico estrella para preparar platos rápidos y con menos grasa. Sin embargo, cuando se trata de recetas tradicionales como la carne adobada, cada cocinero tiene su propia técnica para conseguir un punto óptimo. Entre los creadores de contenido gastronómico más seguidos se encuentra Javier Romero, quien explica de forma muy sencilla cómo es el proceso de preparación en su portal culinario. Para empezar a trabajar con el producto, el cocinero detalla el paso inicial antes de introducir los alimentos en el aparato: "Cortamos las costillas y las ponemos en la cesta de la airfryer". Esta sencilla disposición asegura que el calor comience a actuar de manera uniforme sobre todas las piezas de carne desde el primer minuto. El control de los tiempos es el siguiente factor determinante para evitar que la pieza quede seca o cruda. Siguiendo las indicaciones del chef riojano, el cocinado requiere una pausa a mitad del proceso para remover los ingredientes: "Dejamos cocinar a 180º, durante unos 15 minutos. Después, abrimos, removemos, y las ponemos 5 minutos más". Con este movimiento se consigue un tostado homogéneo por toda la superficie. Por último, más allá de la potencia y la tecnología del electrodoméstico, el éxito de la receta recae fundamentalmente en la calidad de los ingredientes y el tratamiento del adobo. Tal y como destaca el propio Javier Romero para redondear el plato: "En cuanto al sabor, el secreto está en el adobo, que potencia el sabor de la carne". articles.title: Sean Hannity, Ainsley Earhardt marry with Fox News colleagues present
articles.summary: Sean Hannity and Ainsley Earhardt have tied the knot, and many of their Fox News colleagues turned out for the wedding. See the photo and guest list.
articles.body:
Sean Hannity and Ainsley Earhardt have tied the knot.

The Fox News stars were married on Saturday, Oct. 24, their employer has confirmed . According to the network, the ceremony was held at the Church of Bethesda-by-the-Sea in Palm Beach, Florida, where the couple got engaged in December 2024.

"Our hearts are overflowing with love and gratitude as we begin this new chapter together as husband and wife," Hannity and Earhardt said in a joint statement shared with Fox News. "To exchange our vows in our home church where we got engaged, surrounded by our children, families and dearest friends, was more meaningful than we could have ever imagined."

They added, "Our faith has always been at the center of our relationship, and we truly believe God brought us together. We feel blessed by the outpouring of love and support from the wonderful people in our lives and are excited for the future. Above all, we are grateful to God for bringing us to this moment and for the beautiful life we will continue to build together."

Friends, family and colleagues attended the wedding ceremony, including a number of Fox News stars. Per the network, Earhardt's "Fox & Friends" cohosts Steve Doocy, Lawrence Jones and Brian Kilmeade were present, as were Laura Ingraham, Mark Levin, Dana Perino, Bret Baier, Harris Faulkner, Emily Compagno, Bill Hemmer, Martha MacCallum, Kayleigh McEnany, Carley Shimkus and Trey Gowdy.

Other guests included President Donald Trump's son Eric Trump and daughter-in-law Lara Trump, former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, White House deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino and Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis .

Prior to the wedding ceremony, Hannity and Earhardt held a party on Friday, Oct. 23, at Trump's Mar-a-Lago club, which the president and first lady attended.

"I've had a personal relationship with President Trump for over 30 years," Hannity said in a statement to Fox News . "When Ainsley and I began planning this celebration, it was important to us that he could be part of this special time in our lives. We chose to host a party at Mar-a-Lago and paid fair market value for the venue. We are grateful that he and Melania could celebrate alongside our families and friends."

Jason Segel, Ejae, Taylor Swift, more celeb engagements, marriages in 2026

Hannity, 64, hosts his eponymous primetime Fox News show weeknights, and Earhardt, 50, cohosts "Fox & Friends" weekday mornings. Earhardt joined Fox News in 2007, while Hannity has been with the network since 1996.

Hannity and Earhardt confirmed their engagement during the Christmas holidays in 2024. At the time, the couple said they were "overjoyed and so thankful to our families for all of their love and support during this wonderful time in our lives," and they said they received the blessing of their children.

Hannity was previously married to Jill Rhodes from 1993 to 2019. They share two children. Earhardt was married to Kevin McKinney from 2005 to 2009 and to Will Proctor, with whom she shares a daughter, from 2012 to 2019.

During a conversation with USA TODAY earlier this month , Hannity confirmed he and Earhardt had set a date for their wedding.

"I'm engaged to the greatest girl in the world," Hannity told USA TODAY. "And I hope she doesn't change her mind."

In an interview with Us Weekly earlier this year, Earhardt said she and Hannity "prayed and thanked God" after they got engaged in 2024.

"I can't believe God loves me this much to give me the most amazing man I've ever met," she told the outlet. "He's just an amazing, generous, kind, forgiving, loving man who has embraced my child, a 10-year-old. He has children in their 20s, and he's just wonderful."

articles.title: Pep Guardiola, entrenador, y su divertida forma de saltarse la dieta: "Solo sé hacer huevo frito con patatas, soy un artista"
articles.standfirst: El exigente entrenador sorprende al revelar sus dotes culinarias
articles.summary: El exigente entrenador sorprende al revelar sus dotes culinarias
articles.body: Es de sobra conocida por los profesionales del fútbol la disciplina férrea que Pep Guardiola exige a sus jugadores. Unas exigencias culinarias que contrastan de manera radical con las limitaciones como chef que el propio técnico catalán reconoce sin complejos en su esfera más privada. Mientras que en los clubes de élite que dirige se supervisa cada gramo para evitar lesiones y optimizar el rendimiento físico sobre el césped, el director técnico en la cocina es bastante más modesto. Lejos de las sofisticadas dietas de vanguardia que consumen sus deportistas de alto nivel, el que fuera entrenador del FC Barcelona, Bayern de Múnich o Manchester City ha optado siempre por la sinceridad y el sentido del humor al abordar sus propias debilidades gastronómicas, demostrando que la alta cocina y los banquillos de la Premier League no siempre van de la mano. En más de una ocasión, el laureado entrenador ha querido desmitificar la perfección que a menudo se le presupone a las grandes figuras del deporte rey. Frente a los estrictos controles de peso y la prohibición absoluta de alimentos procesados o azucarados tras los encuentros, Guardiola prefiere reírse de su escasa destreza entre fogones. Lejos de la extrema rigurosidad que impone a sus deportistas, él mismo ha confesado con humor qué hace cuando se salta la dieta: "Solo sé hacer huevo frito con patatas, en eso soy un artista". Esta ocurrente declaración que hizo en una entrevista en ElNacional.cat refleja que, a pesar de la presión constante y la tensión táctica de la máxima competición europea, el preparador mantiene los pies en el suelo y disfruta de los pequeños placeres cotidianos más tradicionales. Más allá de la anécdota culinaria, esta faceta desenfadada permite entender mejor el equilibrio personal que busca el técnico fuera de los estadios. En un ecosistema tan exigente como el fútbol moderno, donde la salud mental, el descanso y la desconexión se han convertido en pilares fundamentales para evitar el desgaste prematuro, la capacidad de reírse de uno mismo ejerce como una auténtica válvula de escape. Al final, equilibrar la rigurosidad táctica con la sencillez de un plato casero demuestra que la grandeza deportiva también convive con la más absoluta cercanía humana.

articles.title: Scott Walker’s The Drift will get under your skin
articles.summary: Walker’s 2006 album is unsettling, bizarre, and the perfect way to kill a party.
articles.body: In my mind, Spooky Season music comes in two distinct flavors. There are the fun, occasionally goofy songs like “The Monster Mash” and John Carpenter’s “Halloween Theme.” Then there is the genuinely terrifying: Throbbing Gristle, The Body, or Scott Walker’s The Drift. This 2006 album from the singer-songwriter is truly upsetting. On it, Walker explores death, disease, and tragedy. But not just from some abstract perspective. There are visceral descriptions of the hanging of Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci. He sings about 9/11, his stillborn twin brother, and the Srebrenica genocide. Lyrically, it’s about as dark as an album gets. But it’s the experimental backdrop that drives it all home. [Media: At times, the record sounds more like the score to an Ari Aster film than anything that could be called pop music under even the most generous definitions. Seasick guitars in the verses of “Jesse” give way to dissonant strings that drone oppressively over the chorus. You can feel the low-bitrate MP3 noise that opens “Clara” in your jaw, which also allegedly features the sound of his percussionist punching a pig carcass as part of the rhythm track. Songs stop on a dime, linger in uncomfortable silence, then erupt in bursts of mechanical noise. Animal bleating, foley work, and atonal orchestra sections grind against Walker’s warble. Nothing is ever quite in tune, and it can be challenging to get through the record in a single sitting if you’re not in a very particular mood. But sticking with it can be quite rewarding. Some songs and performances are so beautiful they send shivers down your spine or give you goosebumps. Scott Walker’s The Drift is the opposite of that. You will still have an involuntary physical reaction, but it’s more shudders than shivers. It will make your skin crawl. Scott Walker’s The Drift is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including YouTube Music, Apple Music, Qobuz, Deezer, and Spotify.

articles.title: George Russell admits US Grand Prix pace was ‘rubbish’ as Antonelli closes in on F1 title
articles.summary: The Briton, the pre-season title favourite, finished a disappointing eighth at the Circuit of the Americas
articles.body:
George Russell acknowledged his pace was "rubbish" in Austin on Sunday after he just about stretched the F1 title race to Mexico City next week.

Russell, starting in sixth, was given a five-second time penalty early on at the US Grand Prix for a clash with Oscar Piastri and then struggled for speed, coming home in only eighth place.

Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli , meanwhile, claimed his ninth win of the season and now only needs to finish ninth next week in Mexico to seal his first world championship.

It was another tough Sunday pill for Russell to swallow and the Briton, who was the heavy title favourite ahead of the season, admitted he "does not have the answers" to his issues right now.

"The pace was rubbish today – that's the long and short of it," Russell told Sky Sports.

"Five second [penalty] cost me two or three positions, but the pace wasn't good enough when it needed to be. I don't know – just not being quick enough.

"I need to try and understand why it is. It's strange when you're so far off. Hopefully there's some answers somewhere, but right now I don't have them."

Russell now trails Antonelli by a whopping 123 points with 125 left to play for over the remaining five rounds of the year.

"We are very close," the 20-year-old Italian, who would become the sport's youngest-ever champion, said after his win in Austin. "We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon," Antonelli said.

"I am going to approach with the same mindset – to have fun and fight for another win. Would be best to finish well, that's the goal but just going to try and enjoy the rest of the season.

"I am very happy because I have a very good group of people around me in the team and my father who always comes," Antonelli added.

"A great group of people that help me to be more relaxed and not worry about these kind of things, help me to block out the noise and allow me to enjoy the weekend and perform.

"On Thursday a lot of talk about championship and stuff and I just try to not worry about that and deliver the best result I could. Today was very important for me and the team."

articles.title: Milton Keynes: Why these four people think it's UK City of Culture
articles.summary: The spotlight is shining on the post-war city, after it made the UK City of Culture shortlist.
articles.body:
Milton Keynes has often been dismissed as somewhere not worth pulling off the M1 for, frequently by people who have no plans on visiting in the first place. But recently, that tide has turned. The BBC spoke to four people who have been part of the city's evolution and believe it has a chance of being crowned the UK City of Culture for 2029.

In 2025, the city was named one of the best places to live and work in the UK.

It is now in with a real chance of winning the £10m prize having been shortlisted as one of four places for the City of Culture contest .

The shorthand used to describe Milton Keynes often refers to concrete cows and its many roundabouts.

However, for Irish-born Nigerian creative Maureen Onwunali, who grew up and lives here, the city has so much more to offer.

While researching for her poem as part of the city's original bid, she said she found it "surprisingly so fascinating".

"I devoured all of these facts so now at any party, I have at least five Milton Keynes facts."

City of concrete cows still loved, say residents

In "An ode to Milton Keynes", Onwunali refers to "the colossus, the world's first programmable computer" and "self-driving cars on Roman roads".

She told the BBC: "It's so funny because I tell people about Milton Keynes and culture and they look at me as if I'm being sarcastic, because Milton Keynes has this stereotype of being soulless.

"But there's so many artists who've come out of Milton Keynes.

"A lot do go off to bigger cities like London or Manchester but I think it's just a matter of harnessing their talents and having opportunities to platform them."

'People who live here absolutely love it'

Cultural events already held in the city include Reggae Land at the National Bowl and the Milton Keynes International Festival. This is alongside annual functions held at Campbell Park such as Art in the Park, the Zimbabwe Heritage Festival, MK Pride and Oktoberfest.

On the day the shortlist was announced, a four-month exhibition celebrating the life of British artist Laurence Stephen Lowry opened at the MK Gallery.

Director Anthony Spira said it was "great" that the city's place on the shortlist had surprised people.

"People who live here absolutely love it. But externally, people are saying, 'Milton Keynes, is there culture there?' Well, yes, there is, there's a lot and there's going to be a lot more."

Spira is confident the city, which was born only 59 years ago, can win: "We've got a very different story."

Alongside its gallery, the city is proud of its theatre and live music venue - The Stables - which was developed by world-renowned jazz musicians Sir John Dankworth and Dame Cleo Laine.

The city is also home to smaller creative groups.

The professional theatre company The Play's The Thing was set up by Rosemary Hill in 2008 and encourages new writers and performers as well as producing more traditional plays.

"We've got a fantastic grassroots community doing so many things," said Hill.

However Hill still finds herself having to convince others of her beloved city's charms.

She recalled: "I was sitting on a train a few years ago and was getting off at Milton Keynes and somebody said, 'Oh, this is a place best avoided'.

"I said, 'Have you ever been here? Do you know what Milton Keynes is about. Because you should come and visit and see all these different things.

"The whole carriage clapped as I got off."

'Shining a light on what makes our city unique'

For Lauren Townsend, the deputy leader of Milton Keynes City Council, her connection with the bid is also personal.

Fellow Labour councillor Shanika Mahendran died after a short illness aged just 28 in July.

At her memorial service former council leader Pete Marland revealed she had been the lone voice in the council chamber who persuaded the authority to throw its hat in the ring.

Townsend, who was born and raised in Milton Keynes, said: "Her ambition and belief in our city, combined with the overwhelming support from local people, businesses and organisations, has resulted in us making the final shortlist, and shows just how far our city has come over the past decade.

"I will forever be grateful to pioneers like Shanika for leading the way on a huge opportunity to shine a spotlight on everything that makes our city unique."

The UK City of Culture for 2029 will be announced in early 2027

Milton Keynes, like Wrexham in Wales which is also on the shortlist, was made a city in 2022 as part of the Queen's Platinum Jubilee celebrations.

They are competing with Sheffield and Blackpool with a panel of judges including Grange Hill, Brookside and Hollyoaks creator, Sir Phil Redmond, who will visit each one

Judges will use set criteria to decide the winner, which include how places will create transformative opportunities and richer lives, deliver good jobs and boost growth

Shortlisted cities each receive £125,000 to help with their final bids.

The winner gets a £10m prize. In Bradford, which is the current holder of the title, around 7,000 new jobs have been created, as well as a brand-new performance venue.

articles.title: Amanda Seyfried says she has no regrets about turning down ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’; actor feared film would flop
articles.summary: Actor Amanda Seyfried recalled turning down the 2014 film \"Guardians of the Galaxy\" and said she has no regrets about it.
articles.body: Actor Amanda Seyfried recalled turning down the 2014 film "Guardians of the Galaxy" and said she has no regrets about it.The actor was offered the role of the green-skinned alien assassin Gamora in the Marvel Cinematic Universe film.Seyfried, known for films such as "Jennifer's Body", "Mean Girls", and "Les Miserables", among many others, said the role in "Guardians of the Galaxy" wasn't for her. "I think turning down 'Guardians of the Galaxy' was just so obvious to me at the time," she said in a Q&A session with SAG-AFTRA Foundation."I'm like, 'This is not going to be a hit. The tree and the raccoon are talking to each other. And also they're all in space.' And I was just like, 'This will ruin my career if this is bad. And there's a high chance that this could be bad," she said.The role eventually went to Zoe Saldana.The actor admitted she was "wrong" but has no regrets about the choice. "I mean, obviously I was wrong. But I still don't take back that decision. I made it for myself. I made it for my family that I knew I wanted to have," she said."And I just don't want to spend all the time in the makeup trailer. I just can't sit still anyway. I really don't like stunts, and I don't like heights, and I don't like pretending the entire world. I need something to hold on to," she added.The film went on to earn over USD 700 million at the global box office and has a sequel, "Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2", released in 2017 and another installment "Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3", which released in 2023.The plot revolves around a group of intergalactic outlaws who must team up to save the universe from a fanatical warlord.Seyfried will next feature in "Martha & Muhammad", "Octet" and another installment to "Jennifer's Body", among others.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Tiger Shroff firing incident prompts ASFC to suspend Sunday football celebrity matches featuring Abhishek Bachchan, Ranbir Kapoor and Kartik Aaryan until security arrangements are finalised, club will consult police before resuming
articles.summary: The firing incident involving Tiger Shroff near a football ground in Juhu has disrupted the weekly routine of the All Stars Football Club (ASFC).
articles.body: The firing incident involving Tiger Shroff near a football ground in Juhu has disrupted the weekly routine of the All Stars Football Club (ASFC). Club owner Bunty Walia has cancelled the team’s Sunday practice sessions until further notice, with the matches expected to resume only after the necessary security arrangements are in place. The decision comes amid concerns over the safety of the many Bollywood actors who regularly participate in the club’s football sessions.ASFC suspends Sunday practice after Tiger Shroff firing incidentFor years, Sunday evenings have been reserved for football practice for members of the All Stars Football Club at the Jamnabai Narsee School playground in Juhu. However, the team’s weekly ritual was called off on October 25, following the October 18 incident outside the ground involving Tiger Shroff.According to Mid Day, the incident, in which five to seven bullets were reportedly fired at the actor’s car by two men on a motorcycle, has left the team shaken. The report confirmed that Walia had cancelled the October 25 practice match and would not announce the next session until a security plan was in place.“The October 25 practice match was cancelled by Bunty Walia. He is clear that till a security plan is put in place, he won’t announce the next match. Many actors are part of the ASFC, including Abhishek Bachchan, Kartik Aaryan, and Ranbir Kapoor. Everyone’s safety is top priority,” the report stated.Bunty Walia says ASFC will consult police before resuming matchesWhen contacted by the afore mentioned publication, Walia confirmed that the practice session had been cancelled in the aftermath of the incident. He said the club would need to discuss the way forward with the police before resuming its regular football sessions.“We are not sure about the next practice session. We’ll need to discuss with the police as to how to go forward. We cannot resume till we put the necessary safety norms in place,” Walia said.The case is currently being investigated by the Mumbai Crime Branch. Until the club finalises the necessary precautions, its next practice session remains uncertain.ASFC may keep match dates and venues confidentialAs part of the proposed security measures, the club may also look at keeping its football sessions away from the attention of paparazzi. According to the report, ASFC could keep the dates and venues of future matches confidential to avoid drawing unnecessary attention to the gatherings.The suspension marks a pause in a regular sporting activity that brings together several members of the film industry. For now, the club’s priority is to establish adequate safety arrangements before its celebrity football matches resume.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Toyota’s new GR GT3 to make early debut in Japan next month
articles.summary: Date set for GR GT3’s long-anticipated debut after two public runs at Goodwood
articles.body:
The new Toyota GR GT3 will make its competition debut in Japan next month ahead of a wider rollout in 2027.

Rookie Racing, a team owned by Toyota chairman Akio Toyoda, will enter the Japanese marque's next-generation GT3 car at the SUPER GT finale at Motegi on 7-8 November.

The GR GT3 will replace the squad's regular #32 Mercedes-AMG GT3 in the GT3 division and will compete as an 'open' entry, making it ineligible for points. Two-time Super Formula champion Hiroaki Ishiura and 19-year-old Tokiya Suzuki have been named as its drivers for the double header.

The car will run on Bridgestone tyres, despite Dunlop being selected as the sole supplier for the GT300 class next year when SUPER GT's long-running tyre comes to an end.

Toyota has been developing a GT3 contender under its own brand name for several years, having first shown an early preview of the car at the Tokyo Auto Salon back in 2022.

In July 2025, the GR GT3 made its public debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed, with Haas Formula 1 driver Esteban Ocon driving it up the famous hillclimb. The Japanese manufacturer brought the car back to Goodwood this year, with its World Rally Championship driver Elfyn Evans among those taking it for a spin.

Toyota had been mulling over entering the car at selected races in 2026, with the Nurburgring 24 Hours initially viewed as the ideal race for the car's competition debut. However, that plan did not materialise, but the Japanese marque remained keen on giving its new GT3 racer an outing before the end of the year.

The GR GT3 will be made available to customers starting next year, when it will replace the ageing Lexus RC F GT3. While manufacturers typically limit the availability of new GT3 cars to select teams in the first season, the GR GT3 will certainly race in the World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 division in the hands of the ASP team.

articles.title: Russell says second spot would mean nothing as Antonelli nears title
articles.summary: George Russell says finishing second in the championship would not mean anything as boss Toto Wolff hit back at suggestions that the British driver may never...
articles.body:
George Russell says finishing second in the championship would not mean anything as boss Toto Wolff hit back at suggestions that the British driver may never get another shot at the title.

The 28-year-old trudged home eighth at the United States Grand Prix on Sunday, the bare minimum he needed to keep the title race mathematically alive as leader Kimi Antonelli roared to a dominant victory.

Antonelli now holds a whopping 123-point lead over his team-mate, with Lewis Hamilton still just about in it a point further back. Russell also now has Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc within 10 points of him.

While the Italian is likely to be celebrating the championship in Mexico City next weekend, Russell is not driven by the fight to finish second.

"As long as we win the constructors' championship, that's the main thing," a dejected Russell said.

"Obviously I'd like to finish best of the rest but P2, P3, P5 is not champion, so it doesn't mean anything."

Antonelli was in a league of his own in Austin, romping home a huge 13.0 seconds ahead of Leclerc.

But Russell, hampered by an early five-second penalty, had no answer in the same machinery, unable to get past McLaren's Oscar Piastri to progress from eighth.

"Six good laps, 50 bad laps," Russell added. "The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that's the least of my worries after such a bad weekend.

"He obviously was exceptionally competitive and there are signs that the window (of performance) is very small. I hope that's an explanation for my lack of pace today, but I need to believe in my team because it's difficult to understand when you're so far off."

Russell entered the season as heavy title favourite in the grid's dominant car but his young team-mate has turned the tables and is set to storm to the title.

Former Red Bull motorsport advisor Helmut Marko told Sky Deutschland this week that he doubted Russell would ever get another shot at the championship, having been usurped as Mercedes' number one.

Team principal Wolff hit back at that assertion, saying: "I think he's (Marko) wrong on George. George has all the ability. I think the car doesn't suit him.

"I think that at the beginning of the season it's difficult to cope with a situation where you're feeling like 'this is my year to come', and then you have this wunderkind on the other side that starts to really chip away.

"And I believe that in a new season, George, if we provide him a quick car, has absolutely what it needs to win a championship."

Wolff also believes it is down to the team to understand Russell's deficit to Antonelli, taking blame away from his driver.

"George, for all of us in the team, is a champion and has won in every category. I think he merits to be put in the group of the very best ones," Wolff added.

"This year we see this variability in results. When we land the car in the way that suits him, he's absolutely fine.

"But when it drops out of the operational window, he struggles. He struggles more than maybe Kimi. And that is on us.

"We just have to work it out. Because George is not half a second slower, three tenths slower than Kimi. That's just absolutely not the case.

"So what is it that he doesn't like? What is it that we need to do in terms of modifying the car, setting it up in a different way for him to go fast? Because it's all there - intelligence, ability, determination."

articles.title: Antonelli delivers 'the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet'
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli's Austin win was "the best he has delivered", according to Mercedes boss Toto Wolff, even if it wasn't quite enough to give him the title.
articles.body:
The race that took Kimi Antonelli to the brink of a record-breaking world championship was, in the words of his Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff, "the best he has delivered so far" and "the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet".

The 20-year-old Italian's victory in the United States Grand Prix puts him in an impregnable position.

Antonelli is so far ahead in the points that the only way he could not win the title in Mexico City next weekend is if either his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton win the race. Even then, Antonelli will guarantee the title if he finishes ninth, or 10th if it's Hamilton.

He arrived here thanks to one of the most dominant victories of the season, in a car in which Russell could finish only eighth, albeit hampered by a five-second penalty.

While Russell was toiling and failing to pass McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Antonelli was operating on another level entirely, as he has so often this season.

"Exceptional," Wolff said, "and I think he's outperformed the car."

Antonelli came to Austin already in a strong position in the championship, knowing he would clinch the title if he won with Russell finishing lower than eighth and Hamilton lower than fourth.

He achieved his part of the bargain but Russell and Hamilton did just enough to keep things alive until this coming weekend. Russell was eighth and Hamilton fourth.

Some drivers tighten up when they get this close to achieving their lifetime's ambition. Not Antonelli. He said he was going to treat this like any other weekend, but it wasn't just talk. It's exactly what he did.

"He comes in," Wolff told BBC Sport after the race, in a conversation after finishing his official news conference, "sits on my chair, feet up, and keeps chatting away and saying: 'This is so funny. I'm not thinking about the championship at all.' And in a kind of youngish excitement, almost like it's surreal. And that's why it's not so important."

Did Wolff think that was because Antonelli's lead was so large that he had no need to feel any pressure, or was it innate?

"The advantage helps," he said. "But it's also innate in him and I don't think that it's something to be trained for. He's not over-thinking it."

Wolff's claim about this being Antonelli's best performance so far might surprise anyone who watched him win his home grand prix at Monza from 19th on the grid.

When this was pointed out, Wolff replied: "My problem is that I don't remember past races. So now you're saying Monza was actually also pretty good, obviously with the advantage of the home crowd and seeing all these tifosi that were a little bit confused, wearing red, and an Italian with the Mercedes outfit up on the podium. And I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Mercedes caps next year.

"So both of them were pretty good. But the headline that this is the best we can keep."

Antonelli agreed. "Monza, we clearly had the fastest car," he said. "We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back. But it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick.

"Definitely, Monza was a super-special one, and one that I will remember forever. But this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good."

Mercedes went to Austin with both cars in the new upgraded specification that had proved unconvincing, to say the least, when it made its debut in Malaysia two races ago.

There, Wolff said he thought it had made the car 0.3secs per lap slower. The team split the cars in Singapore to try to understand the package better, and then used it on both cars in Austin. Antonelli stuck it on pole and dominated the race. Russell's performance looked more like the one the car produced in Malaysia.

"The update we put on the car is difficult to operate," Wolff said. "And Kimi landed it.

"Maybe it's a bit harsh to say but I think his driving style just glues with the car. We saw that in qualifying yesterday where on his last lap he could have been another 0.15-0.2 secs up. And on the other side George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult."

When Antonelli clinches the title, he will become the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari in 1953. It's a remarkable statistic for a country which is so engrained in the sport, and it certainly resonates with his compatriots.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "As an Italian, wow, we need to go back to Ascari, the names that they created the inspiration for all of us. To see an Italian achieving this level of performance and results in Formula 1, that's particularly thrilling, as an Italian person in motorsport."

Stella's answer continued into an area that begins to explain the way in which he has proved so superior to Russell this year.

"Going more into the technical, and specifically this season, Kimi is a very interesting one to look at, because he pretty much attacks all the times," Stella said.

"You see how often he's just going off track, and you see his onboard (camera), he's pretty aggressive. But at the same time, this seems to be not only kind of an aggressive driving, or an attacking driving, but effective.

"And if we think how much we talk in these media sessions about the cars being difficult to drive consistently fast, it should be recognised how much he's been able to harness his driving style with what is required of the cars.

"But at the same time, almost contradicting what I'm saying, when is the time to bring home the result, he's been able to do it.

"So he's the deserving leader of this championship. He's writing an important piece of history for motorsport, because once he achieves the championship, he will be the youngest."

Antonelli will beat by more than three years the previous record for youngest winner of the championship, Sebastian Vettel in 2010.

As with the title itself, he is aware of the forthcoming achievement, but not letting it affect him.

"I'm going to approach it with the same mindset," he said. "Just trying to have as much fun as possible, trying to hopefully fight for another win.

"It would be best to finish on a high, and that's the goal. But I'm just going to try to enjoy the rest of the season from now on."
authors: Andrew Benson - F1 Correspondent in Austin
